title: question
description: A change waiting for a yes, the same answer for every app (ADR-S04, G-STACK-13): with no terminal a command answers it instead of changing anything, HTTP gives it with 428 and the CLI exits 3. A reader decides by its kind, shows detail, and sends the same request again with the id and a yes. Its data is defined once here; its wrapper follows the contract version the reader asked for, ran on envelope/v1 and source on envelope/v2.

apiVersion.description: Always elderlygate/contracts/question/v1: the one form of the question, the same for every app, so a reader knows its shape whatever it asked for.

kind.description: Always Question, so a reader tells a change waiting for a yes from every other answer by kind alone.

data.description: What the change is and how it asks.

id.description: A one-time id for exactly this request, so a yes binds to the change it was asked for: the app remembers the method, path, flags, body sum and type, keeps it a few minutes, and takes it once. A yes sends it back (confirm=<id>, or --confirm <id>). It is no trace id.

action.description: The change's type, the words every product shares (G-STACK-13), so a reader can remember the answer per type.

system.description: True for a change to the system itself (uninstalling, removing a token, dropping data, deleting a board), which asks for the name whatever the user picked (G-STACK-6).

style.description: How this change asks, as the command worked it out from the user's choice: type_name (type the name) or yes_no (y/N).

detail.description: What will change, in plain words for a person, with no CLI wording such as pass --yes, so the page and the terminal show the same question.

errors.description: Always empty: a change waiting for a yes is not a problem (ADR-S21).
